proxy_language: Proto-Nilo-Saharan / Proto-Eastern Sudanic / Proto-Nubian (reconstructed), with Old Nubian (attested ca. 8th-15th c. CE) and Nobiin as the nearest attested daughter-language proxies
proxy_rationale: The Sebilian is a Late Pleistocene/Epipaleolithic lithic industry (ca. 13-11 ka) of Kom Ombo/Upper Egypt-Nubia, with no linguistic record. Any language link is hypothetical: the Nile Valley of Nubia is the historical homeland of Nubian languages (Northern Eastern Sudanic), but Proto-Nubian is dated only to ca. 2-3 ka BP at best, and the Sebilian long predates it. Real affiliation of the Sebilian people is unknown (could even be Afroasiatic or an extinct isolate). Proto-Nubian/Old Nubian is used purely as a regional, phonologically coherent stand-in. Weak link; treat as stylistic, not historical.
phonology: Proto-Nubian (Bechhaus-Gerst, Rilly): consonants roughly p b t d c j k g (plus w, y), nasals m n ny ng, liquids l r, fricatives s, f (marginal), and h in loans; vowels i e a o u with length contrast (a/aa etc.). Old Nubian (written in Greek-based alphabet with Coptic letters) shows b d g k t p s m n l r w, palatal ny/y, velar nasal ng, vowels a e i o u, plus long vowels. Nobiin has a contrast of geminates and a velar nasal, and implosive-like d. No aspiration, no breathy-voiced or ejective series, no 'dh/kh/th/xh' contrasts of the kind in current game names.
phonotactics: Predominantly open or closed CV(C) syllables; words typically 2-3 syllables, roots often CVC(V). Onsets are single consonants; initial consonant clusters are essentially absent (clusters arise only across syllable boundaries, e.g. -ng-, -rk-, -lt-, nasal+stop). Word-final: vowels or sonorants/stops; Old Nubian nouns often end in a vowel or in -l, -n, -r, -s, -k. Verb forms end in suffix vowels. Vowel harmony not robust; stress is lexical or penultimate/initial (poorly attested), without effects on spelling.
orthography: Scholarly transliteration of Nobiin/Old Nubian in Latin script: ordinary Latin letters, ny for the palatal nasal (or ñ), ng or ŋ for the velar nasal, long vowels written doubled (aa, ee, ii, oo, uu), y and w as glides, j and c as palatal affricates (Nobiin c, j). Use no h-digraphs for aspiration (avoid th, dh, kh, ph, bh, xh). Reconstruction notation: asterisk-marked Proto-Nubian forms in Rilly's and Bechhaus-Gerst's style.
morphology: Agglutinating, mostly suffixing, SOV language type. Nouns: roots plus suffixes for case (Nobiin nominative -ø, accusative -ka/-g, genitive -n(ti), locative/dative -ki/-gi, instrumental -ti(n)), definiteness/number (plural -ti, -i, -ri, -ki variants; Nobiin plural -ti, -i, -ri), and a few derivational suffixes (-in, -kil, -gi/-ki, -si; agent suffix -kal in Old Nubian; Nobiin -kiri). Verbs: root plus tense/aspect/person suffixes; some prefix-like clitics. Reduplication occurs for intensity/plural in some Nubian roots. No noun-class system in Nubian proper (traces of noun-class prefixes may exist in Eastern Sudanic more broadly). Case marking only at the end of the noun phrase.
compounding: Compounds are head-final: modifier + head (N-N, with the head last). The genitive precedes the head: possessor + (-n/-in linker) + possessed, e.g. X-n Y 'Y of X'. Attributive adjectives and relative clauses usually follow or precede nominal head depending on the language; Old Nubian places adjectives after the noun, but genitives and compounds go before the head. Agent compounds: object + verb root + agent suffix (e.g., water-carry-er). A name like 'Temple of the Sun' = Sun-GEN temple, e.g. 'wer-in kor'. Avoid inventing precise morphology: use short roots plus simple genitive -n/-in linker, plus -kal/-kiri for agent.
noun_phrase_order: Possessor-GEN precedes head noun; modifier compounds precede head; adjectives follow nouns in Old Nubian (N Adj), demonstratives and numerals precede/follow variably; case-marking and plural suffixes attach to the last word of the NP.

attested_roots.gloss: river? (Old Nubian; possible loan from Greek/Arabic Nile)

notes: Strictly speculative: the Sebilian industry (Nubia/Upper Egypt, ca. 13-11 ka BP) predates any reconstructable language; Nubian is a regional stylistic proxy only. The current game names (Ngikparhu, Mbopge, Dhoxir, Tjosthu, Huthu) use aspirated/prenasalized clusters (ngikp-, mbo-, dh-, tjo-, -thu) that are not Nubian-like; prefer short CV(C)(V) words, 2-3 syllables, ending in a vowel or in l/n/r/s/g/k, with ny/ng only medially or finally. No word may be identical to a Modern Irish, Scottish Gaelic or Manx word, as Nubian is not Goidelic; avoid accidental matches with Irish (e.g. 'ar', 'mal', 'nil', 'kab' are short and may collide, so extend or inflect them: ar-in, mal-ti, wer-kal). Attested Nubian forms above are given from memory in simplified scholarly transliteration and some glosses (kor, kab, tir, mal, nil) are uncertain; verify in Browne's Old Nubian Dictionary or Werner's Nobiin grammar before treating as authoritative. Worked examples are left empty rather than inventing unverifiable morpheme sequences; the compounding rules above (head-final, genitive -n/-in, plural -ti, agent -kal) can be used to build names such as 'aman-in ki' (house of water) or 'wer-in ar' (great sun) as stylized approximations.
